At a height of 6 ft 3 in (1.91 m) tall, he played at both the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. ==High school== Grundy began his high school career at [[Warren Central High School (Kentucky)|Warren Central High School]], in [[Bowling Green, Kentucky]], where he played for [[American Basketball Association|ABA]] legend [[Darel Carrier]]. During his senior year, Grundy left to play for Scott Shephard and Kevin Keats at [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, VA]]. ==College career== Grundy initially signed a letter of intent to play for Bradley University as a junior in high school. After pleading his case to Bradley administrators, the university granted him his release. Grundy visited several schools before committing to [[North Carolina State University|NC State]], where he played [[college basketball]] with the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]]. Initially just a bench role player, he was named 1st Team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] during his senior season. That same season, he became the 1st player in school history to lead his team in 5 major statistical categories (Scoring, Assists, Rebounds, Steals, 3-pointers made). Grundy also earned All-ACC-Defensive-team honors in 2002. == Professional career == Grundy played with the [[National Basketball Association]]'s [[Atlanta Hawks]] in 12 games after signing a ten-day contract in the [[2005–06 NBA season]]. Grundy's final NBA game was played on April 19, 2006, in a 99 - 100 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] where he recorded 2 points, 2 assists and 1 rebound. He played in the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian league]] with [[Teramo Basket|Siviglia Wear Teramo]] in the 2006–07 season. On July 12, 2007, he joined [[Panellinios BC|Panellinios]] of the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]].[http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14418/448/item ULEBCup.com Grundy signs with Panellinios.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715122532/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14418/448/item |date=July 15, 2007 }} He was the [[List of top scorers in Greek Basket League by season|Greek League's top scorer]] during the 2007–08 season, averaging 21.5 points per game. In 2009, he joined [[Basket Club Ferrara|Ferrara]].[http://www.solobasket.it/news.asp?id=4635 Biennale per Grundy a Ferrara (Italian).] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722053805/http://www.solobasket.it/news.asp?id=4635 |date=July 22, 2011 }} In September 2010, he returned to Greece, signing with [[AEK Athens B.C.|AEK Athens]]{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20100908002602/http://www.thehoopsmarket.com/news/aek-athens-signs-anthony-grundy.aspx AEK Athens signs Anthony Grundy]}} He left the team on January 15, 2011.[http://www.basketblog.gr//pages/viewcontent.aspx?e=i&l=1&p=3&c=130&i=63499&t=1&w=0 Τέλος ο Γκράντι]{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} {{in lang|el}} In January 2011, he signed with [[Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi S.K.|Mersin Buyuksehir]].[http://www.basketfaul.com/?islem=2&makaleID=5774 Mersin'e skorer Amerikalı] {{in lang|tr}} On July 15, 2011, he was signed by the [[Petron Blaze Boosters]] as a replacement import for the injured [[Jeremy Wise]].[http://www.pba.ph/news/entry/1043 Grundy joins Boosters] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717092617/http://www.pba.ph/news/entry/1043 |date=July 17, 2011 }} He was able to lead the Boosters win the [[2011 PBA Governors Cup]] over the [[Talk 'N Text Tropang Texters]]. In 2012, he signed with [[Mahram Tehran]] of Iran.[https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/basketball.aspx?NewsID=290068 Anthony Grundy agreed terms with Mahram to play in Asia Cup] In 2013, he joined [[Hacettepe Üniversitesi B.K.|Hacettepe University]]. He then began training in the practice sessions of the Greek team AON Palatianis. ==Legal issues== In 2011, Grundy was arrested and charged with [[driving while intoxicated]] (DWI) for the fourth time. He remained at large until 2017, when he was arrested in [[Queens, New York]], while entering the United States. Grundy had lived in [[Ghana]] for several years prior. He was sentenced in October 2017, to two years in prison for a felony charge of DWI, five misdemeanor counts of failing to appear in court and two probation violations.{{cite news|last1=McDonald|first1=Thomasi|title=Former NC State basketball star's 'bad run' ends in prison sentence|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/crime/article179310521.html|access-date=8 December 2017|work=[[The News & Observer]]|date=October 17, 2017|language=en}} On June 6, 2019, Grundy struck and killed a pedestrian and left the scene of the accident, then later turned himself in to police. He had no driver's license nor insurance at the time of the collision, while his license plates had expired the previous year.{{cite web | title=Former Warren Central basketball player turns self in after fatal hit-and-run | website=WBKO | date=2019-06-15 | url=https://www.wbko.com/content/news/Former-Warren-Central-basketball-player-turns-self-in-after-fatal-hit-and-run-511353801.html |
